T.r: The Fighters' Guild. We take contracts the watch won't: beasts, raiders, old doors that need emptying. Beds upstairs for members.
The Mages' Guild. Ingredients, relics, errands that need a spell at the end of them. There are beds if you've nowhere else.
I came from Villemont, 34 years back. I'm a smith. If I want anything it's to hear from my daughter.
I'm a smith. Nails, mostly. Everyone wants swords; everyone needs nails.
Not anymore.
Born here. 6 years, man and boy. I'm a armourer. If I want anything it's a quiet year.
I'm a armourer. The same as my mother did, and hers.
Niamh: "Carry this to Elder Cormac at Droichead, north-west of here. Put it in their hand, no one else's." (56 gold.)
I came from Marnbrouey, 20 years back. I'm a apothecary. If I want anything it's to be left alone, mostly.
I'm a apothecary. The same as my mother did, and hers.
I came from Ruins of Villeargent, 10 years back. I'm a trader. If I want anything it's to go to sea again.
I'm a trader. The same as my mother did, and hers.
I came from Trodou, 42 years back. I'm a trader. Married to Tadhg, 3 children. If I want anything it's to hear from my daughter.
Tadhg. 3 children, and they eat like it.
56 gold. The town won't forget it.
Born here. 14 years, man and boy. I'm a trader. If I want anything it's a quiet year.
A brother somewhere. We don't write.
Born here. 3 years, man and boy. I'm a innkeeper. Married to Bríd. If I want anything it's to be left alone, mostly.
I'm a innkeeper. Beds, ale, and other people's trouble.
Bríd. No children. We tried.
Born here. 8 years, man and boy. I'm a innkeeper. If I want anything it's one good harvest, just one.

Niamh: "Carry this to Harbour Reeve Róisín at Portclare, east of here. Put it in their hand, no one else's." (47 gold; 59 if it is done by Weaverday, the 13th of Reaping. After that, the work goes to someone else.)
There’s one other guest in tonight. A room is 11 gold — the second door on the right, a bed, a bolt on the door, and breakfast if you’re up for it. Will I make it up for you?
11 gold, and thank you. The second door on the right, up the stairs, and yours till this time tomorrow. The other doors aren’t mine to open, nor yours either.

D.text: The room you let is the innkeeper’s again.
A letter for Harbour Reeve Róisín — for Mayor Niamh: 59 gold if it is done by then; after it, the work is taken back.
The Giving — the year’s dead named at the old gate.
